seed.note: at most two random cotangent seeds per test; no test repeats the same check over several fixture seeds

precision: float64 for every central-difference and Taylor check
float32 for the CUDA adjoint comparisons with precision-dependent steps

physics_configuration.epsilon_and_shape: tests/test_differentiable.py: 16x15x1 cells, 0.1 um, 3 CPML cells, float64 CPU, 35 steps, objective mean of signal squares, sphere radius and centre through smooth_sphere_epsilon; Taylor remainder at h = 1e-3, 5e-4, 2.5e-4 along the fixed direction (0.4, -0.3, 0); central difference h = 1e-5 on the radius; explicit adjoint against full autograd on cpu and cuda (seed 82), central difference h = 1e-5 on a scalar epsilon design with nonuniform mesh and one-way plane sources
physics_configuration.epsilon_pmc: tests/test_pmc_general.py gradient_scene: 10x6x6 cells with PML/PMC/PEC faces, 14 steps, float64, random epsilon seed 3 and random direction seed 11; central-difference step sweep h = 4e-3, 2e-3, 1e-3
physics_configuration.ade_coefficients: tests/test_pmc_dispersive.py: epsilon_inf, spatial strength, omega0 and gamma with directions scaled by each parameter's mean magnitude (seed 11), sweep h = 4e-2, 2e-2, 1e-2; tests/test_dispersive_adjoint.py: order-one leaves times scales (1, 1e30, 1e15, 1e15), central difference h = 1e-4 along (0.2, -0.3, 0.4, 0.1) in float64 on cpu and cuda; geometry-to-ADE sigmoid density Taylor remainder at h = 2e-3, 1e-3, 5e-4; tests/test_cuda_dispersive_adjoint.py: CUDA float64 density shift, strength and gamma Taylor at h = 4e-3, 2e-3, 1e-3 with torch and fused backward
physics_configuration.modal_objective: tests/test_mode_adjoint_oracle.py: modal S objective, float64, 600 steps, cpu and cuda, direction seed 3, h = 2e-3, 1e-3, 5e-4
physics_configuration.density: tests/test_density_layer.py: density 4x3 through the density-to-epsilon map (torch.autograd.gradcheck) and an FDTD directional derivative with central difference h = 1e-5
physics_configuration.shape_parameters: tests/test_shape_gradients.py: 19 polygon parameters through the fill VJP (no FDTD), random direction seeds 3 and 5, central difference h = 1e-5, Taylor at h = 1e-3 and 2.5e-4; vertex and control-point gradients through the checkpointed adjoint, float64 CPU, 18 steps, central difference h = 1e-5
physics_configuration.source_waveform: tests/test_source_parameters.py: scalar waveform parameters of gaussian_waveform against independent finite differences, float32 step 2e-3 and float64 step 1e-5 (no FDTD)
physics_configuration.directional_driver: tests/test_cr_directional_check.py: benchmarks/cr_spectral_objective.py check_density_direction on a synthetic objective with Rademacher direction seed 1729 and steps 2e-3, 1e-3, 5e-4
physics_configuration.pml: 3 to 4 CPML layers in the FDTD fixtures; part of the differentiated operator

reference_method: Full Torch autograd through every time step (small-problem oracle), central differences of the same discretisation at one or several steps, first-order Taylor remainder ratios under step halving, and random directional VJP seeds; all of validation layer A by construction. Nondimensionalisation: leaves are order one and scaled by characteristic magnitudes (1e30, 1e15 rad/s), fields divided by dt or steps times dt, gradients rescaled by (1, dt^-2, dt^-1, dt^-1) and finite-difference directions scaled to the parameter magnitude.

observables.name: adjoint_versus_autograd
observables.definition: explicit adjoint gradient against the full-time autograd gradient

observables.name: central_difference_error
observables.definition: |central difference - directional derivative| / |directional derivative| at each step of the sweep

observables.name: taylor_remainder_ratio
observables.definition: R(h)/R(h/2) with R(h) = |f(x + h d) - f(x) - h g.d|

observables.name: directional_vjp
observables.definition: VJP along random cotangents against the reference path

central_difference.sweep_pmc: errors[-1] < 1e-6 |d| and errors[0] > 3 errors[1] > 9 errors[2] (second order until round-off)
central_difference.sweep_pmc_dispersive: errors[-1] < 1e-5 |d| with the same ratio chain

taylor_remainder.superlinear_only: ratio < 0.3 per halving (modal, branch, tensor rotation), R(h/4) < R(h)/8 (polygon)

acceptance_limits.density_gradcheck: torch.autograd.gradcheck float64 on the density map; FDTD directional derivative rtol 2e-6, atol 1e-9
acceptance_limits.source_of_limits: repository-recorded budgets; the program's float64 discrete limit rtol 1e-7 is met by the adjoint-versus-autograd checks (1e-9 and tighter) and by the single-step central differences (1e-6 to 2e-6 relative, which is the finite-difference truncation floor, not a solver discrepancy)
